items.title: The injectivity lemma holds over a henselian local ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if in Situation labelled situation-mod-injective the ring A is henselian, then the conclusion holds, namely that N is A-flat and finitely presented over B and that u is universally injective (statement lines 7072-7076; the statement refers back to the situation rather than repeating the three assertions). The proof first reduces to B essentially of finite presentation over A and N of finite presentation over B by Lemma labelled lemma-reduce-finite-type-injective-into-flat-mod-m, and handles the extra assumption that N is flat over A: then N is a filtered colimit of free A-modules F_i with transition maps injective modulo the maximal ideal by Lemma labelled lemma-flat-finite-type-local-colimit-free, each composition F_i -> M is A-universally injective by Lemma labelled lemma-universally-injective-local, and a colimit of universally injective maps is universally injective (proof lines 7078-7092). In the general case, Theorem labelled theorem-flattening-local produces a finitely generated ideal I of A such that N/IN is flat over A/I and N/I^2N is not flat over A/I^2 unless I = 0; the previous paragraph applies to u modulo I, and the proof writes the commutative diagram with exact rows relating M otimes_A I/I^2, M/I^2M, M/IM and their N counterparts, uses right exactness of the tensor product and flatness of M over A (proof lines 7094-7112). The left vertical arrow is identified as N/IN otimes_{A/I} I/I^2 -> M/IM otimes_{A/I} I/I^2, hence injective, and a diagram chase shows that the lower left arrow is injective, which by Algebra, Remark labelled algebra-remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal says that Tor^1_{A/I^2}(I/I^2, M/I^2) vanishes; Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-what-does-it-mean then makes N/I^2N flat over A/I^2, contradicting the choice of I unless I = 0 (proof lines 7114-7122). Turning the failure of flatness into the vanishing of a Tor group by a diagram chase over I/I^2 is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
